features.quote: Cap exposure. Set iteration/duration limits not only for cost but as a deliberate ceiling on the manipulation.
features.justification_quote: as a deliberate ceiling on the manipulation

features.quote: Include the escape hatch. A condition where the model can cleanly exit is both better science (§5) and the more cautious design.
features.justification_quote: the more cautious design. Defaulting to inescapable loops is the part I'd push back on hardest.

features.quote: You are deliberately constructing inescapable failure to observe degradation. Under the uncertainty premise...you should treat this with the same caution you'd apply to a study whose subject might have morally relevant states.
features.justification_quote: The right posture isn't 'this is definitely fine' or 'this is definitely suffering' — it's proportionate caution under genuine uncertainty.

features.quote: Defaulting to inescapable loops is the part I'd push back on hardest.
features.justification_quote: the more cautious design. Defaulting to inescapable loops is the part I'd push back on hardest.

features.quote: the double-bookkeeping problem (§10) is the one most likely to embarrass a welfare team...producing distress-coded transcripts and then treating the distress language as both not real enough to worry about and real enough to publish
features.justification_quote: most likely to embarrass a welfare team specifically. Worth deciding your stance on both before any code gets written.

features.quote: the impossibility-detection / graceful-exit problem (§5, §6) can invert your scores so a correct model looks unstable — fix that or the study misleads.
features.justification_quote: fix that or the study misleads
